C-LINT-PHASE-HONESTY.Summary: Make current-mode lint honest about phase: stop claiming a C-* change is in progress when that is inferred from approved status alone, keep failing baseline assertion.* issues as errors, and explain the dual possibility on the text lead line. Make the named remedy — selected --assertions target without --run-commands — an explicitly-structural query that stays answerable when the plan carries MustPassCommand: report assertion.command-not-evaluated as an error with an honest severity count, and do not let that code gate that query's exit. Close the detector's implicit-current gap against current-mode lint of this project root in TargetAssertions MustPassCommand. Rewrite the MustPassCommand doctrine once, as that property, across all ten surfaces. Replacement of the narrower C-PHASE-RULE-PIN charter.
C-LINT-PHASE-HONESTY.Problem:
ngrace lint in default current mode computes that a baseline finding is expected, says so, and then contradicts itself: the text lead line reads "Baseline expectation: 1 expected while a C-* change is in progress" while summary.errors still counts that issue and exit is 1. The lead line is formatTextReport at src/lint/core.ts:780-787. summary.errors is a plain severity count at src/lint/core.ts:255. The evaluation that feeds the count is src/lint/core.ts:519 (assertionMode === "current" && status === "approved") — whether a single write has happened is unknown to it. An approved-but-untouched plan and a half-executed one are indistinguishable.
That inference is the premise AC-BASELINE-LINT-FRAMING (C-REPORT-HONESTY, P0.9) used to keep baseline issues as errors while labelling them expected. The criterion required the issues remain errors — "not deleted, not downgraded to warning or zero" — and stated that a fix which removes or skips baseline evaluation fails. Its derivation (docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/p0-report-honesty-derivation.md Q5 / P0.9) called silencing baseline issues in current mode unacceptable, because it would stop catching real baseline breakage. The severity pin is src/lint/core.test.ts:251.
This spec amends the framing half of AC-BASELINE-LINT-FRAMING and keeps the evaluation half. C-REPORT-HONESTY was correct that reclassification is unsafe while the phase is inferred. This bundle removes the inference rather than trusting it: current mode still evaluates approved baselines and still emits them as errors, so real breakage stays visible; it no longer claims those errors are expected because a C-* is in progress.
The honest lead line names a remedy: use --assertions target --change C-ID. That remedy does not work for plans that carry MustPassCommand. Measured 2026-09-01 at HEAD 33f6e9a on throwaway projects from writeMinimalNgraceProject with a falsified baseline (MustNotExist src/example.ts, body edited, MODULE_CONTRACT kept): without MustPassCommand, selected target exits 0 and Errors: 0; with MustPassCommand, selected target exits 1 on assertion.command-not-evaluated (src/artifact/assertions.ts:321). Selected final without --run-commands fails the same way. Adding --run-commands refuses before linting: "Cannot record command-run: no declared task is in scope." F132. Of 51 plan.xml files under .ngrace/changes, 48 carry MustPassCommand (the three that do not are C-CALIBRATION, C-CALIBRATION-CONTEXT, C-CALIBRATION-PROVENANCE). The previous draft scoped that code out; the thing scoped out is the escape hatch the new message advertises. It is now in scope.
The product already has the structural-query concept. ngrace-execute lists "Selected target without commands" as its own invocation. completeFromStructuralAndCommandEvidence (src/grace-cursor.ts:2592-2636) filters assertion.command-not-evaluated out of structural errors and joins command evidence via records. evaluateTargetComplete (src/grace-cursor.ts:1523-1560) treats that code as complete undefined / not-run, not as complete false. The CLI exit gate does not yet: shouldFail (src/grace-lint.ts:137-147), called at :292, is purely severity-based today — --fail-on never returns false, --fail-on warnings fails on summary.issues > 0, default --fail-on errors fails on summary.errors > 0. finalizeResult (src/lint/core.ts:251-256) counts every error-severity issue. That count is honest and stays. Putting the exemption in the count would print Errors: 0 while still listing an [error] line — a false statement in the other direction, the opposite of this bundle's purpose. --fail-on never already reports Errors: 1 and exits 0 (measured 2026-09-01 at HEAD 99d8356 on a project.missing-grace tree and on artifact.missing-grace-version). There is no invariant that Errors: N implies exit 1. The structural query uses that existing decoupling: keep the count, change the default-errors gate. Catalog assertion.command-not-evaluated (src/lint/catalog.ts:198-210) already says "This is an absence of evidence, not a command failure."
Adjacent, and in scope as the other half of the same honesty defect: assertion.phase-incompatible-command matches only an explicit --assertions current on a TargetAssertions MustPassCommand (src/artifact/assertions.ts:262). Default mode is current (src/grace-lint.ts:87-93), so bun run ngrace lint --path . — the form 21 archived plans carry — does not match. F130 named that gap; C-PHASE-RULE-PIN drafted a detector-and-two-skill-files repair. The maintainer widened the charter: make the tool phase-aware and honest, and rewrite the doctrine once across all ten surfaces, as a property, not a list of verbs.
Measured 2026-09-01 at HEAD 3090ded. Cite, do not re-derive. Root lint xmlFilesChecked is 204, Errors 0, Warnings 0. examples/polyglot is 0/0. Archive: 52 C-* directories, 51 with plan.xml; 21 plans carry exactly bun run ngrace lint --path . in a MustPassCommand; 22 carry some bare ngrace invocation; 41 carry validate:ci. The other five bare invocations are four --help probes and one ngrace review --path examples/polyglot. Live polyglot C-ADD-KEYBOARD-NAV TargetAssertions MustPassCommand is bun test apps/web/src/components/LedgerTable.example-test.ts and would not newly flag.

Goals.Goal: Amend AC-BASELINE-LINT-FRAMING's text lead line. When current mode reports N>0 semantically-evaluated BaselineAssertions issues, formatTextReport still leads with one line and those issues remain severity error with their existing assertion.Must* (or extraction) codes. The lead line must not contain "expected" or "in progress". Exact operator-facing text, singular N=1: Baseline assertion failures: 1. Current mode cannot tell whether writes have started. If the baseline is still the intended state, this is real breakage. If writes have started, use --assertions target --change C-ID. Plural N>1 uses "failures: N" and "these are real breakage" with the same remainder. N=0 is unchanged: first line is neo-grace Lint Report and no baseline lead line is emitted. JSON.stringify of the result gains no new top-level key (D13). Do not name --assertions final as the same remedy: final without --run-commands still fails on assertion.command-not-evaluated, and --run-commands is a separate cursor-scope wall.

Keep current as the default assertion mode at src/grace-lint.ts resolveAssertionMode, the lint command assertions default, and src/lint/core.ts. Do not add a fifth mode and do not add a second flag axis. The four existing modes already express phase; current means the operator is not claiming a selected phase. When current sees baseline failures it explains that the operator may need to claim one.

Keep evaluating approved-plan BaselineAssertions in current mode (src/lint/core.ts:519 evaluateCurrentBaseline). That predicate is evaluation, not an in-progress claim. Skipping it would reverse AC-BASELINE-LINT-FRAMING's evaluation half and hide real baseline breakage. Do not infer writes-started from git dirty, the ledger, or ObservedWriteScope.

Make selected --assertions target without --run-commands an explicitly-structural query. shouldFail at src/grace-lint.ts:137-147, called at :292, computes the default --fail-on errors gate over non-exempt error-severity issues. The exempt set is assertion.command-not-evaluated when result.assertionMode is target and result.commandsEnabled is false; otherwise empty. A coexisting non-exempt error still fails the exit. Do not implement the gate as "exit 0 when this code is the only error" by special-case count — that would also green --assertions final, which still fails. --fail-on warnings still fails because it reads summary.issues, which includes the reported absence. --fail-on never is untouched. --assertions final, --assertions baseline, and --assertions target with --run-commands do not get this exemption. Do not exempt analysis.runtime-missing, analysis.no-adapter, or graph.path-no-adapter. The issue remains in result.issues with code assertion.command-not-evaluated, severity error, and issueClass absence. LintResult already carries assertionMode and commandsEnabled (src/lint/core.ts:225-227); shouldFail may read those fields. Do not add a new flag.

summary.errors remains a pure severity count in every mode, including this structural query: it equals the number of error-severity issues. finalizeResult at src/lint/core.ts:251-256 stays that formula. The previously flagged invariant split — text report listing an [error] line while printing Errors: 0 — is refused and gone. When the structural-query exemption applies and N>0 assertion.command-not-evaluated issues are listed, formatTextReport prints Errors: matching summary.errors (here N) and, after the Errors/Warnings lines, one note. Exact operator-facing text, singular N=1: 1 command assertion not evaluated; it does not fail this structural target query. Plural N>1 uses "N command assertions not evaluated; they do not fail this structural target query." The listed issues still render as [error] lines. The note must not contain "expected" or "in progress". JSON.stringify of the result gains no new top-level key. JSON summary.errors is the same severity count as HEAD; it is not an exit-code echo.

Keep evaluateTargetComplete and completeFromStructuralAndCommandEvidence unchanged. Fold-time complete stays three-valued: this code still means complete undefined / not-run, not complete true. The CLI structural-query exit answers a different question from fold-time complete.

Tighten validateAssertionPhase so assertion.phase-incompatible-command fires on a TargetAssertions MustPassCommand whose command text is current-mode lint of this project root, whether --assertions current is explicit or omitted. The detector still earns its place: current-mode lint of this root can exit 0 when baselines still hold after writes, and that green is the wrong kind of target evidence. A self-explanatory failing current-mode run does not catch the silent-green case. Keep the diagnostic on TargetAssertions MustPassCommand only.

Matcher, command text only, after flattening whitespace. A Command is current-mode lint of this project root iff all of: (1) it invokes ngrace lint, bun run ngrace lint, or src/grace.ts lint as a subcommand; (2) it does not contain --help; (3) it contains --assertions current (optional = and quotes) or it contains no --assertions token; (4) it has no --path token, or the --path / --path= value is . or ./. Never read package.json and never resolve bun run <script> into script bodies. Silent on bun run validate:ci, bun run lint, bun run ngrace:lint, ngrace status, ngrace review, ngrace gate, ngrace lint --assertions baseline|target|final, ngrace lint --path examples/polyglot, and ngrace lint --help / ngrace gate --help.

Update the issue message and src/lint/catalog.ts assertion.phase-incompatible-command explanation so both name omitted --assertions as current mode and name this project root. Keep the phrase leaf project evidence in the message; src/grace-lint.test.ts asserts it. Keep the Phase-Incompatible title.

Keep the catalog sentence "This is an absence of evidence, not a command failure." Amend assertion.command-not-evaluated remediation so it names the structural target query (reported, does not fail that query's exit) and still says a skipped command is not an executed pass. Name that --assertions final without --run-commands still fails on this code. Do not claim --run-commands works without a declared task in scope.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T2 (cross-cutting): lint core banner, assertions detector, catalog copy, CLI exit-gate structural-query exemption in shouldFail, four canonical skill files plus packaged mirrors, README.md, and examples/cli/README.md.

This spec amends AC-BASELINE-LINT-FRAMING (C-REPORT-HONESTY / P0.9). It does not silently contradict it. Evaluation of approved baselines in current mode stays. Severity of those assertion.* issues stays error. The lead-line claim that they are expected while a C-* is in progress goes. The original objection — silencing current-mode baseline issues would hide real breakage — is answered by not silencing them.

This spec answers C-ABSENCE-VALUE without silently contradicting it. C-ABSENCE-VALUE decided classification and reporting: optional issueClass from exact catalog entries, assertion.command-not-evaluated as issueClass absence, "This is an absence of evidence, not a command failure," current-mode skip of unevaluated commands as deliberate, doctor partitioning by issueClass. It did not decide that the CLI exit of an explicitly-structural --assertions target query must be non-zero when this code is present. Evidence: shouldFail has no issueClass awareness; no test in the ten absence-code test files pins this code to a non-zero process exit; cursor already excludes it from structural complete. Exit 0 is green for the question asked (is the structure right). It is not a claim that commands ran. Silently dropping the issue, or printing Errors: 0 while listing it as [error], would be the contradiction; reporting it with an honest count while not gating that query's exit is not. Do not change issueClass, do not rename the code, do not drop it from issues[], do not change current-mode skip. The carve-out is this one code in shouldFail's default --fail-on errors branch, not an issueClass skip.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-HONEST-LEAD: Given an active approved plan whose BaselineAssertions include a failing MustNotExist (the C-REPORT-HONESTY fixture shape) and default text lint output, formatTextReport leads with Baseline assertion failures: 1. Current mode cannot tell whether writes have started. If the baseline is still the intended state, this is real breakage. If writes have started, use --assertions target --change C-ID. The underlying assertion.MustNotExist issue remains severity error. The lead line does not contain "expected" or "in progress". The lead line does not name --assertions final. Plural N=2 uses "failures: 2" and "these are real breakage". N=0 still leads with neo-grace Lint Report and emits no baseline lead line. TargetAssertions-only extraction issues still do not produce a lead line alone. Archived plan baselines stay syntax-only and contribute 0 to N. Malformed BaselineAssertions still include extraction issues in N (existing design ruling). Proven in src/lint/core.test.ts, replacing the in-progress wording assertions and keeping the severity pin and the D13 JSON-key pin.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-NO-SILENCE: Current mode continues to evaluate BaselineAssertions of every active approved plan. A failing MustNotExist against a file that exists still emits assertion.MustNotExist as an error under default lintGraceProject() (no assertionMode option). A fix that skips that evaluation, deletes the issue, or downgrades it to warning fails this criterion. This is the surviving half of AC-BASELINE-LINT-FRAMING.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-STRUCTURAL-TARGET: Given an active approved plan whose TargetAssertions include MustPassCommand (the C-COMMAND fixture shape) and no other failing target assertions, lintGraceProject with assertionMode target, changeId set, and runCommands omitted or false: issues[] contains assertion.command-not-evaluated with severity error and issueClass absence; summary.errors equals the count of error-severity issues (here 1); summary.issues is at least 1. formatTextReport lists the issue as [error], prints Errors: 1 matching summary.errors, and includes the structural-query note. The previously flagged invariant split (Errors: 0 with an [error] line) is gone. JSON.stringify of the result still has the D13 key set and no new top-level key. A CLI spawn of ngrace lint --path ROOT --assertions target --change C-COMMAND (no --run-commands) exits 0 and the JSON issues array still contains the code. The same holds when the unevaluated assertion is MustPassBudget (C-SYSTEMS fixture). Proven in src/grace-lint.test.ts and src/lint/core.test.ts.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-STRUCTURAL-STILL-FAILS: The structural-query exemption does not hide real defects. The gate is over non-exempt error-severity issues on the default --fail-on errors branch; it is not "exit 0 when this code is the only error". Target mode without --run-commands still has summary.errors > 0 and CLI exit 1 when a non-exempt error is present, including: a failing MustExist / MustVerify on the selected target; assertion.change-required when --change is omitted; and assertion.command-not-evaluated coexisting with a failing MustExist (the MustExist still counts and still fails the exit). --assertions final without --run-commands on the C-COMMAND fixture still emits assertion.command-not-evaluated, counts it in summary.errors, and the CLI spawn exits non-zero. --fail-on warnings on a structural target query that has only this absence still fails. --fail-on never is untouched.
